references.text: Joseph says that Pharaoh's dreams are one and the same dream, and that God has shown Pharaoh what he is to do – a direct parallel to verse 28.
Joseph explains that the dream was repeated twice because the matter is firmly decided by God, and God will soon bring it about – emphasizing that it is God who acts.

Daniel explains that there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries and has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the last days – a parallel to Joseph's interpretation that God shows Pharaoh the future.
The Lord God does nothing without revealing his plan to his servants the prophets – the principle that God reveals his plans to people.
The psalm mentions the famine and Joseph's role, and that the word of the Lord tested Joseph – the broader context for God's plan revealed through Pharaoh's dreams.
Direct theological parallel: Both verses use identical wording ('show what I will do') to emphasize that God reveals his plans before they happen.
Direct narrative and theological connection: 45:8 interprets and completes the meaning of the prophecy mentioned in 41:28.
